newsitem.title: USA: GE raises dividend, boosts buybacks, sets stock split.
newsitem.headline: GE raises dividend, boosts buybacks, sets stock split.

text.p: In a widely expected move, conglomerate General Electric Co. Thursday increased its quarterly dividend and share repurchase programme and announced a 2-for-1 stock split.
GE's board voted to boost the quarterly dividend 13 percent to 52 cents a share from 46 cents a share, marking the 21st consecutive year of increased dividends by GE.
The dividend is payable on Jan. 27 to shareholders of record as of Dec. 31, the company said.

GE also increased its share repurchase programme from $9 billion to $13 billion and extended the programme through 1998. This allows GE to continue its daily stock purchases at an annual rate of $3 billion to $3.5 billion through 1998.
GE has bought back 92 million shares valued at $6.3 billion on the open market during the past 24 months under the share repurchase programme that began in December 1994.
GE said it expects the repurchases to increase the company's earnings-per-share growth rate and return on equity.
The stock split, which will be voted on at the April 23, 1997 annual stockholders meeting, would be GE's second in the past three years and fourth in the past 14 years.

"The strong performance and future outlook of our diverse mix of leading global businesses -- combined with their high level of cash generation -- enables the company to increase dividends in line with earnings and extend the share repurchase programme ... through 1998," GE Chairman John F. Welch said.
"GE's strong cash generation also allows the company to build for the future by continuing its record levels of internal investment and making complementary acquisitions for its businesses."
GE's stock rose $3 to $102 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
